headline: More professional firms asking TL Telecoms for a quote
told: You want more enquiries, and you want them now
Customers find you mostly through ads and online
You sell to businesses and to the public, with a team of 2 to 10 people

today.step: A firm's phone bill feels too high

today.leak: Form asks for a message, not their setup
No time given, so they ask others too
No date kept to come back to them

future.note: Every quote and contract end date kept
On the day their contract ends

noticed: You're really clear about who you're for: law firms, accounting firms, medical practices and other professional firms. Most telecoms sites try to talk to everyone
Your pricing is published and simple, month to month with no contracts and per-second billing. That's a real strength, and most of your competitors hide it
The quote form asks for a name, company, phone, email, the service and a message, but nothing about how many people they have, who they're with now, or when that contract ends
The site says you respond quickly but not how quickly, and the WhatsApp number is there but easy to miss on a phone
There are no client stories or reviews yet, so a cautious firm has nothing from someone like them to go on
planTitle: How we would go about it

plan.title: Go to the firms, not just wait for them
plan.body: Your best clients aren't searching for a new phone system, they're just paying too much for the one they have. So we'd reach out to law, accounting and medical practices with roughly 5 to 30 staff, starting in KZN and Gauteng, in your name, with one simple message about what they're paying and per-second billing.

plan.title: A quote form that does the work
plan.body: Ask the few things you need to price it: how many people, how many lines, who they're with now, roughly what they pay, and when that contract ends. Add a WhatsApp button that's always visible, and a line that says when they'll hear back.

plan.title: Show the saving fast
plan.body: Every quote request answered within your working hours with a rough saving against what they pay now, so they don't go and get two other quotes while they wait.

plan.title: Never lose a not-yet
plan.body: Most firms will be mid-contract. Every quote and every contract end date goes into one simple pipeline, so you're the one who calls them the month their contract runs out, not whoever happens to be in front of them that week.

plan.title: Something to point to
plan.body: Once the first few firms are on, a short line from each one on the site and in the messages, because a law firm trusts what another law firm says.

timeline.label: Quote form, first reply and pipeline
timeline.body: You approve everything as we go

timeline.label: Outreach to professional firms
timeline.body: Normally when the new conversations start coming in

timeline.label: Follow-ups and contract-end call backs
timeline.body: Tuned every month from what the numbers show

worth.title: Why it's worth it

stats.label: a month for a 10 person firm on your own published pricing: 10 hosted extensions, 2 SIP channels and basic voice recording, excluding VAT and call charges
a year from that one firm, and you keep earning on every call they make

worth.body: And because you're month to month, every firm you bring on keeps paying until they have a reason to leave. Twenty firms like that is over R15,000 a month coming in before a single call is billed.

next.title: Talk it through
next.body: It would really help to know roughly how many quote requests you get in a month, how many of those turn into clients, and what a typical client looks like for you, number of people and lines. Then I can show you exactly where the biggest gap is.
